label: prf:q-logarithm-exists
title: Proof of existence of the $q$-logarithm primitive
html:
Proof. Proof of existence of the q-logarithm primitive

By Milnor--Moore, \mathrm{Prim}(\mathcal{H}_q) is the Lie algebra of the grouplike group G(\mathcal{H}_q), so the formal inverse of \exp_q exists as a primitive whenever \exp_q is bijective onto its image. Explicitly, over R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]\bigl[\tfrac{1}{[n]_q} : n \ge 1\bigr]

  \log_q(1 + x) \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{(-1)^{n-1}  x^n}{[n]_q}

is primitive (verified by \Delta_q(x^n) and cancellation) and inverse to \exp_q (verified by the q-binomial inversion). Over \mathbb{C} this recovers the convergent series (q-logarithm). Over \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{C}_p existence follows from the corresponding \exp_q existence via the Milnor--Moore adjunction.
